function: Channel acquisition (joint estimation and prediction) of the MIMO-OFDM channel from outdated past channels plus a small pilot-based partial estimate of the present channel (pp. 1, 4).
system: Massive MIMO-OFDM: BS with 32 antennas (ULA; 8x4 UPA in appendix) serving single-antenna users, 32 subcarriers, 3.5 GHz, 40 MHz; no RIS (pp. 3, 9, 13).
method: Supervised: complex-domain MLP-Mixer (CMixer) with LSTM (RCDNet) or transformer encoder (ACDNet), trained offline with MSE loss, Adam, and data augmentation (pp. 6-9).
data_channel: Open-source ray-tracing DeepMIMO 'O1' outdoor scenario, BS3, 3.5 GHz; 3000 training sequences, 20000 mobile and 20000 quasi-static test sequences from different user areas (p. 9).
test_conditions: Same O1/BS3 scenario for training and testing, with disjoint user areas; test split into mobile and quasi-static sequences; input-disturbance sweep; UPA variant in appendix (pp. 9, 11, 13).
baselines: Learned only: CMixer-based channel-mapping estimation [17] and LSTM-based channel prediction [23]; no classical (LS, MMSE, interpolation) baseline compared (p. 10).
metrics: NMSE and cosine correlation rho between acquired and true channel; pilot-overhead reduction up to 88.9% (pp. 1, 10).
complexity: Order O(S^2 n + Nc Nt^2 + Nt Nc^2 + Nt Nc S n) for RCDNet (Table I); FLOPs: RCDNet 194.89M, ACDNet 373.51M, LSTM 170.03M, CMixer 17.57M (pp. 8-9).
openness: none (no code or data link of its own; relies on the public DeepMIMO dataset, p. 9)
q1_support: p. 9: "we use opensource raytracing-based DeepMIMO scenarios and datasets" (DeepMIMO ray tracing, scenario 'O1').
q2_support: p. 9: "We collect the training and test data in different areas of the scenario to avoid data leakage" - a held-out split of the same O1 scenario and BS3; no other scenario, band, antenna setup, or adaptation is tested with a trained model.
q3_support: p. 10: "One is the channel estimation enhanced by CMixer-based channel mapping" and "The other is the channel prediction based on an LSTM network [23]" - both benchmarks are learned; a non-learned baseline is missing.
q4_support: p. 8: "the computational complexity of RCDNet is O(S 2 n + Nc Nt 2 + Nt Nc 2 + Nt Nc Sn)"; p. 9: Table III lists "FLOPs of RCDNet" as "194.89 Million".
q5_support: p. 9: "we use opensource raytracing-based DeepMIMO scenarios and datasets" - trains and tests on the public DeepMIMO channels; the paper gives no link to its own code.
notes: PDF is the arXiv v2 preprint (2403.19409v2) titled 'Channel Deduction: A New Learning Framework to Acquire Channel from Outdated Samples and Coarse Estimate'; the DOI is not printed in it, matched by topic and venue. Pages 11-15 have no extractable text and were read as images. q2 is borderline: train and test user areas are disjoint (p. 9) but belong to the same DeepMIMO O1 scenario, so it is treated as a held-out part of the same data; the sizes of the known present channel, the number of past channels, and the UPA appendix are not stated to reuse a trained model. q3: both benchmarks (CMixer mapping, LSTM prediction) are learned networks. q1 and q5 rest on DeepMIMO ray tracing (confirm). Fine-tuning is only mentioned as future promise (p. 10).
